lina: FYI ran into a weird parity issue in the C# sampleapp: on retry the exported span's request_id becomes <redacted> even though the initial attempt had the real id
marco: interesting. which Http stack and retry handler are you using?
lina: HttpClient with a DelegatingHandler-based retry (Polly). minimal ordering in Startup: 

lina: ```csharp
app.UseOpenTelemetry(); // Activity/OTel propagation
app.UseMiddleware<RedactMiddleware>(); // scrubs headers for logs/wire
// Polly retry DelegatingHandler registered on HttpClientFactory
```

lina: Behavior: first request log -> request_id=rid-77; retry triggered -> logs show request_id=<redacted>; exported span attribute request_id also shows <redacted>
tasha: could be that Polly replays the same HttpRequestMessage instance and our RedactMiddleware mutated headers after Activity tags were lazily resolved by the .NET OT exporter at export time
rohan: .NET Activity API often copies tags at export but some exporters read header collections on export lazily depending on instrumentation. That can lead to this race when middleware mutates headers later
marco: does the C# sampleapp set Activity.SetTag("http.request_id", val) eagerly when the incoming headers are parsed?
lina: currently we parse headers and leave them on HttpContext.Request.Headers, and rely on the Otel instrumentation to pick them up. not setting an explicit Activity tag
tasha: suggestion: snapshot the header into an immutable tag immediately in our OpenTelemetry middleware: Activity.Current?.SetTag("redwood.request_id.orig", headerVal) and mark it sensitive for exporters. this avoids any downstream mutation affecting the span attr
rohan: agree. alternative: run redaction at the last possible moment (wire-level) instead of mutating shared Request.Headers earlier. but with DelegatingHandler the retry may happen inside HttpClient, so middleware ordering is hard to control for outbound requests
marco: also note that in some app servers the logging middleware runs before our Otel middleware, so logs might show different values depending on registration order. language parity matrix needed
lina: i prototyped the snapshot tag and added a unit test that simulates retry by re-sending the same HttpRequestMessage after RedactMiddleware runs. test asserts Activity tag contains original id and exporter payload has redacted attribute only if configured to redact at export
tasha: nice. exporter-side safeguard still needed: add a processor that strips or hashes any attribute matching a sensitive_keys list before sending to OTLP/Jaeger. prevents accidental export if we miss a snapshot somewhere
rohan: small security note: if we add a snapshot tag name like redwood.request_id.orig, treat it as sensitive metadata in source control & telemetry docs. ensure the exporter scrubber can be toggled & audited
ina: (oops typo) lina: i mean thanks, rohan :)
marco: docs action: i can add a row in devex/telemetry docs: "C# (ASP.NET) - Polly/DelegatingHandler: retry often replays request instance; snapshot header -> immutable span tag; wire redaction last" plus short snippet and unit test example
lina: i opened WIP PR in sampleapp: https://git.internal/redwood/sampleapp/pull/7890 - adds snapshot tag + test + feature flag to enable exporter-scrubber for dev/test only
telemetry-bot: New issue opened: DEVEX-5108 "csharp sampleapp: request_id mutated on retry when redaction runs after retry" - https://issuetracker.internal/DEVEX-5108
rohan: i'll follow up with an exporter PR to add the sensitive-attribute scrubber behind a feature flag; i'll also add an e2e test that runs the sampleapp against a test OTLP collector and asserts no raw ids in payloads	asha: one more note: add a short "hook ordering checklist" in the devex doc so integrators can scan for common patterns (middleware vs DelegatingHandler vs filter). that'll help new SDK users avoid this pitfall
lina: assigning: marco -> docs; rohan -> exporter scrubber; tasha -> sampleapp tests; me -> sampleapp PR owner. will link PR & ticket in the doc. thanks! :thumbsup:
